name: extended_data
description: Use when standard OBD2 PIDs are not enough and you need the car's manufacturer values: oil temperature, EGR position, DPF figures and the like.
instructions: Call read_extended {} to read the first 8 DIDs this car's profile declares, or name up to 8 declared DIDs, e.g. {"dids":["1707","1708"]}.
Each line is "<did> <name>: <value> <unit>"; only DIDs the profile declares are read, an undeclared one is named and skipped.
For a diesel particulate filter question use the dpf skill (read_dpf): it reads the same DPF DIDs and adds the assessed status.
Read a value once with read_extended; to see one change over time, ask about it with standard PIDs in read_live or record_live instead.
interpret: These DIDs are manufacturer-specific and read on the engine ECU's default addressing; the decoding comes from this car's profile.
A value marked unconfirmed comes from a DID not yet checked on this car: treat it as indicative, a lead to confirm, never as proof of a fault, and never base an urgent verdict on it.
"no answer" means the ECU did not return that DID (not supported, or another ECU holds it): it is not a fault.
Compare a value with what standard PIDs say where they overlap (e.g. oil temperature against coolant 0105 on a warm engine): a large disagreement points at the decoding, not the engine.
